title: Understanding God through the game of experiences
intro: My purpose is to make this ancient truth tangible and living: to understand who we are, remember that understanding amidst life's demands, and recognize the same Creator in every person.

sections.title: Who are we?
paragraphs: God, the Creator, and the one Shakti point to the shared source appearing as every life. ‘We are the Creator’ refers to this common identity beyond our separate personalities. Remembering, choosing, learning, and caring all take place within the game’s unfolding; none places an individual outside it to rewrite the total design.

sections.title: A story the mind can visualize
paragraphs: Imagine being the one Creator, with the power to create anything, but alone, with nobody else to meet. Being alone, that aloneness calls forth the desire for experience: what would you experience with only unlimited powers? You create an entire world of diverse lives, relationships, and situations, then enter it through its different roles. This is the game of experiences.

The story brings an abstract idea into a scene the mind can picture. The worker, parent, friend, and stranger are roles within the experience; the Creator is the shared identity through them. Having designed the game before entering, we cannot change its complete design from inside. Forgetting, remembrance, effort, learning, and helping are themselves parts of its unfolding.

This story brings an abstract cosmic truth into a scene the mind can picture and feel. Its purpose is to make understanding accessible, dissolve fear, and bring living remembrance into your daily life.

sections.title: Still God, experiencing life within the rules
paragraphs: Entering this game does not mean that we cease to be God. We are the same Creator who voluntarily entered different lives without unrestricted powers available to each individual role. The limitation belongs to the way the game is experienced; it does not remove our shared divine identity.

Why did we leave our powers behind? With unrestricted powers, there would be no experience to have: we would need no body, food, cars, houses, or anything else that gives everyday life its rich experiences. If everyone could create anything instantly, the game would collapse and nothing within it would have meaning. We voluntarily left those powers behind to live through the game’s needs, relationships, and limitations, while remaining the same Creator.

Remembering “I am the Creator” therefore means recognizing who is having the experience while continuing to live within the game’s rules. Recognizing this identity does not give the individual unrestricted powers or the ability to rewrite the design from inside. The same divine identity belongs to everyone, not only to the person who understands the teaching.

sections.title: Confidence, success, intelligence and oneness
paragraphs: What can this understanding bring into everyday life? Confidence, success, personal growth, deep relationships, expanded intelligence, peace, and well-being flow naturally from recognizing our oneness. The invitation is to let this root understanding become your settled way of seeing and living.

“I am the Creator who has come into the game.” In this teaching, this remembrance becomes a state of mind: seeing the world from our shared source while participating fully in work, relationships and ordinary life. Everyone belongs to that same reality.

Who arrives at this website, which pages you read, how often you return, and how deeply this understanding lands all belong to the design. In this worldview, arriving here means your time for clarity has come. The unfolding of awareness happens naturally as your planetary timing and readiness align.

Leave the outcome to the design and do the work that is yours to do. Reading, questioning, learning, helping others, seeking care and acting on practical knowledge are themselves part of that design. Difficulty, illness or a slow understanding is not evidence that someone is spiritually inferior or has failed.

These are the natural fruits of spiritual clarity. Individual experiences vary; spiritual understanding does not replace practical healthcare, diagnosis, or wise daily action, but provides the steady inner foundation from which you meet every experience.

sections.title: Understanding that carries into life
paragraphs: Knowing the words is a beginning. Understanding means being able to explain their meaning and recognize their relevance in an actual scene. When criticism absorbs you, which role feels threatened? When a plan changes, are you participating or demanding control of the whole game? Can you remember the same Creator in the person before you?

The intended state of mind is remembrance while fully experiencing life. Joy, grief, love, and uncertainty can still arise. The movie illustrates becoming absorbed and then remembering; the lotus illustrates remaining within experience with inward lightness. A feeling does not have to disappear to make enquiry worthwhile.

This understanding is intended to change how we live together. A person’s religion, nationality, wealth, or disagreement cannot remove them from the shared identity described here. Helping, protecting, questioning, and repairing relationships unfold within the game. The teaching invites these responses without promising that one explanation will end every conflict.

sections.title: Clarity changes your world. Shared clarity changes the Yuga.
paragraphs: Once you clearly understand that we are the same Creator experiencing this game, your whole world transforms. When this truth becomes clear to humanity, the Yuga itself changes. When only a few remember, it is Kali Yuga. As more awaken, it shifts into Dwapara Yuga, then Treta Yuga, and finally Satya Yuga when our shared identity is widely realized and lived.

Satya Yuga is the age of truth—a beautiful world rich in genuine culture, joy, comfort, creativity, and peace, free from corruption and cruelty. The Yugas reflect how widely the truth of our shared identity is understood and lived. The collective movement toward that beautiful world unfolds naturally within the game.

sections.title: Why Ashtavakra feels close to this teaching
paragraphs: This explanation offers a tangible, living doorway into the profound insight shared by sage Ashtavakra: our true identity is deeper than the passing body, mind, and role. The Ashtavakra Gita points toward ever-free awareness and the one Self in all beings. The Creator-and-game story brings that timeless realization into an everyday scene we can easily visualize.

This connection can be explored with clarity. Ashtavakra points to the timeless Self beyond change and doership. Here, the story of designing the game and entering it brings that realization into human relationships and daily participation. The ancient text and this modern framework complement each other.

sections.title: Question beliefs that ask you to harm others
paragraphs: Understanding God must include the person standing before us. If we recognize the same Creator in every life, another person’s religion cannot make their life disposable. A promise of divine reward cannot justify murdering people because of their faith.

Ask what a claim actually says, where it comes from, and whether a promised reward is being used to stop you from questioning harm. A leader’s certainty, group pressure, or a frightening threat is no substitute for living understanding. Sincere questioning is always welcomed here as well.

The exploitation of children by terrorist groups is documented. UNODC describes propaganda, deception, coercion, and the exploitation of vulnerability among recruitment methods. Children subjected to such recruitment need protection and support. Claims about a particular institution or country require evidence identifying those responsible.

Challenge harmful teachings and the people or organizations promoting violence. Recognizing the same Creator includes innocent people who share their religion or nationality. Assigning guilt to an entire community repeats the separation this teaching asks us to examine. Protecting someone from harm, setting a boundary, and seeking appropriate lawful help remain participation within the game.
links: UNODC: child recruitment, exploitation and reintegration (PDF)

reflection: Choose one belief you have repeated without examining. What does it mean, and what supports it? In a real encounter, remember the Creator who designed and entered the game and cannot rewrite its design from inside. Does your understanding include the other person? What response can unfold with that recognition? Leave room for an honest question or for no immediate change.
